title: Cardiovascular system: heart and vessels
note: cardi/o means heart; angi/o and vas/o mean vessel; arteri/o is artery; ven/o and phleb/o are vein. Prefixes on card/i name its parts: endocardium (inner lining), myocardium (heart muscle) and pericardium (the sac around the heart).

read.title: Layers, chambers and vessels
text: The heart is a muscular pump with four chambers. The two upper chambers, the atria, receive blood; the two lower chambers, the ventricles, pump it out. The right ventricle sends blood through the pulmonary circulation to the lungs, and the thicker left ventricle drives it through the aorta to the rest of the body. Valves between the chambers keep blood moving in one direction.

Prefixes do much of the naming. With card/i or cardi/o as the root, endocardium is the inner lining, myocardium is the muscle of the heart wall, and pericardium is the sac around the heart. Add -itis and you have inflammation of each one.

Vessel terms come in sets. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins return it, and capillaries are the tiny vessels where oxygen and nutrients pass into tissues. Angi/o and vas/o both mean vessel, so angioplasty repairs a vessel and vasodilation widens one. Phleb/o and ven/o both mean vein; a phlebotomy opens a vein to draw blood.
Diagnostic terms combine the same parts. An electrocardiogram records the heart's electrical activity, while an echocardiogram uses sound waves to make an image of it.
